title: What If a T. Rex Chased You? The Movies Got It Wrong

scenes.text: What if a T. rex chased you? The real speed is not what movies show.
Older guesses said it could hit 45 miles an hour, faster than a car on a city street.
But a 2002 Nature study found its leg muscles were too small for that. The estimate: about 11 miles an hour.
A 2017 computer model agreed, about 12 miles an hour. Any faster, and its leg bones would shatter.
Usain Bolt covered one stretch of his record sprint at 27.8 miles an hour, more than double that.
So the jeep chase is fiction. A six-ton T. rex was built for power, not for sprinting.
